provenance_note: The reference corpus was authored by an independent agent without access to the tool code, and this run recomputes every check from the shipping build.
reference: Corpus for the generic barrier-based causal engine of spec 17. Synthetic scenario packs (imported as JSON, neutral graph: conditions, hazards, initiating events, barriers with condition dependencies, pathways with barriers in series order) with tri-state setup values and ordered run decisions; expected pathway statuses (open / blocked + blocked_by / no_hazard / not_initiated / review) derived by ref.py through exhaustive possible-world enumeration of unknowns, cross-checked with Kleene K3 logic; plus pack/replay refusals, and three property cases per built-in scenario (all barriers in place, all absent, all unknown). 8 randomized packs, seed 20260916. Values 'true/false/unknown' map to the README tri-states yes/no/unknown and in place/absent/unverified; setup keys H*=hazard present, E*=initiating event occurs, B*=barrier in place, C*=condition holds.
reference_citations: tools.petrov.re spec 17 Safety Scenario Lab (MVP scope, model rules, validation, acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common section 0.5 and acceptance list
README-safetyscenariolab.txt rule statements SSL-ENG-001..009 (input vocabulary and stated engine rules only)
Kleene strong logic of indeterminacy K3 truth tables, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-valued_logic (section Kleene and Priest logics)

M. Johnson, M. Manton, C. Cowley, M. Scanlon, 'Bow Ties in Risk Management; using the new CCPS-EI book to avoid pitfalls', IChemE Symposium Series No 163, Hazards 28, 2018, https://www.icheme.org/media/16937/hazards-28-paper-31.pdf p.3
tolerance: All checks exact: statuses, blocking barrier names, counts and refusal flags are categorical/integer and the engine performs no numerical computation (all-or-nothing barriers, no probabilities), so identity is the only meaningful criterion. '_positive' means > 0; 'status_is_X: false' means any status other than X.

not_benchmarked.Scenario content: Content correctness of the 10 built-in scenarios against NFPA 51B, EN 1004-1, OSHA 1910.147/1910.253, HSE INDG455/HSG107, IEC 60364, ISO 12480-1, Directive 2003/10/EC: the tool cites them at document level without clauses or limits, and the pack item ids are not visible to an independent author; only structural properties are checked.
not_benchmarked.Named barrier after an unknown: Which barrier is named when an earlier barrier is unknown and a later one effective (case unknown-before-effective checks only blocked-or-review).
not_benchmarked.Non-open statuses: Status when unknowns change only between non-open results (e.g. hazard unknown with an effective barrier): only 'not no_hazard' and 'not open' are asserted.
not_benchmarked.Interface properties: Visual gate, screenshots, no-text-in-drawing, alt text, list view completeness, keyboard operation, PDF layout, seven-language strings: UI properties, not reproducible from an independent reference.
not_benchmarked.Probabilistic branch: Probabilistic branch and seed replay: not implemented (post-MVP), README states no random branch.
not_benchmarked.Exchange document: Exchange document scenario.outcomes field shape and localStorage behaviour: framework plumbing, no independent reference.

coverage: Engine rules SSL-ENG-001..009 (no hazard, not initiated, dependencies with K3, first effective barrier, open, unknown->review, decision override and sequence, validation refusals, no safe claim), the blocked-vs-no-hazard debrief distinction, data-driven import of new scenarios (all synthetic cases are imports), JSON replay round trip and tamper detection, and reachability of open/review states in each of the 10 required scenarios.

self_test.note: window.__safetyTests(): engine rules, golden replays, branch enumeration, visual gate, asset and seven-language checks.
